Infectum exists after round 1, so this is new meaning/context, not a new box. The m- belongs to the stem formation; -i-lan indexes plural agent and first-person plural patient, not Detransitive voice.

The hostile group context supports stronger contact/overwhelming than gentle tapping; one example does not establish the precise degree of injury or a literal destruction sense. No new fixed idiom is established.
Are mtaptap and mṭapṭəp phonological variants of one verb, and is the t/ṭ contrast source-specific? The single new occurrence cannot determine this.

Is Mṭapṭəpilan conventionally beat us up, trample us, or overwhelm us, and how productive is the stronger use relative to gentle mtaptap/mṭapṭəp?
